lead.headline: India's stocks rebound as the AI trade unwinds and foreign funds return
signal: Foreign flows into India are driven partly by money leaving AI-heavy markets, not only by India's own fundamentals. If the AI trade re-strengthens, that support could fade.
lead.hook: The MSCI India index has ==rebounded 11% from an October low==, adding more than $400 billion in value and almost erasing this year's losses.
points: India lost ground in the first nine months of the year because the AI trade pulled global investor money towards AI-linked markets.
As that trade unwinds, India's small AI exposure has turned from a weakness into an advantage.
Global funds are turning more positive on India's $5.4 trillion equity market as oil prices retreat and earnings growth accelerates.
The 11% gain is measured from a six-month low set in October.
lead.editors_read: India's rally is a relative trade: money is leaving crowded AI positions and India has little AI exposure to sell. Cheaper oil and faster earnings give funds a domestic reason to stay. If oil turns up or AI stocks recover, the same flows can reverse quickly.

frontpage.headline: Trump, Putin and Xi plan a joint meeting in China next week, White House says
signal: Any arms deal needs China, which has no treaty history with the US and Russia. If the meeting yields only a statement of intent, the no-limits situation continues.
frontpage.hook: Trump, Putin and Xi plan a three-way meeting at the Apec summit in Shenzhen next week, with nuclear arms reduction on the agenda but no agreement expected.
points: The White House says Trump will raise cutting nuclear weapons. Iran may also come up, but Ukraine will not. Russia has confirmed the meeting; China has not yet reacted.
A senior US official said no agreement is expected from the talks.
The US-Russia nuclear treaty expired in February, leaving the two largest arsenals without major limits.
Trump wants a better replacement that includes China, which is building up its arsenal. Former US officials told the BBC this could take years.
Trump will also hold bilateral talks with Xi, their fourth meeting since he returned to office in 2025.
frontpage.editors_read: The meeting is a signal, not a deal: the US wants China inside the next arms framework, and Beijing has little reason to accept limits while its arsenal is growing. The risk is mainly for the old US-Russia limits, which nobody has replaced. Watch whether China publicly confirms the trilateral session at all.

frontpage.headline: India-US trade pact near the 'finishing line', Jaishankar says
signal: If the deal is signed around the G20, exporters get clarity on tariffs. Until the US settles its legal basis for tariffs, any rate agreed remains exposed to change.
frontpage.hook: External Affairs Minister Jaishankar says the bulk of issues in the India-US trade deal, including tariff lines, are resolved and talks are at the 'last stretch'.
points: He says the remaining concerns are mostly on the American side. India wants a balanced deal that gives its goods an edge over comparable economies.
Talks began in early 2025. An interim deal on February 2 would have cut US tariffs on Indian goods to 18% from a combined 50%, which included a 25% penalty over Russian oil.
On February 20 the US Supreme Court struck down Trump's global tariffs. Trump then imposed a temporary 10% tariff under the 1974 Trade Act, leaving the status of the deals unclear.
Rubio said last month the sides were 'about as close as you can be'. Sitharaman had said on October 5 that talks hit a 'plateau'.
Modi is likely to meet Trump at the G20 in Miami on December 14 and 15.

frontpage.headline: India's deep-tech funding is growing, but startups need more buyers, says Kris Gopalakrishnan
signal: If large Indian firms buy more startups, deep-tech investors get earlier exits and may fund more early-stage companies.
frontpage.hook: Infosys co-founder Kris Gopalakrishnan says Indian deep-tech startups are finding more capital but too few acquirers, so investors still wait 10 to 12 years for exits.
points: Indian startups mostly exit through public listings, and the path from founding to exit can take 10 to 12 years.
A more active mergers and acquisitions (M&A) market would give investors an exit before an IPO and shorten that wait.
Indian companies have traditionally built technology in-house. He sees more acquisitions now but says firms must take more risks.
He suggests buyers could finance deals with private equity partners or debt.

frontpage.headline: India's household inflation crosses 6% while growth stays strong
signal: Higher rates make loan EMIs costlier. If tightening goes too far, it could slow the growth the RBI is trying to protect.
frontpage.hook: India's CPI inflation rose to 6.09% in October from 5.54% in September, above the RBI's 6% upper limit for the ==first time since October== 2024.
points: It was the twelfth straight monthly rise, driven by food prices and a base effect (prices compared with a low level a year earlier).
The RBI raised its repo rate (its lending rate to banks) by 25 basis points to 5.5% last month. Economists expect another hike at the December 2-4 meeting.
BofA Securities expects a further 75 basis points of hikes over the next six to nine months.
The RBI forecasts inflation averaging 6% in October-December and 5.7% in January-March 2027. GDP grew 7.8% in April-June, which keeps demand high.
Risks: crude oil prices and El Nino, which could hurt crops and food supply.

frontpage.headline: Asian governments react to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's exit
signal: Governments are treating Nvidia as critical infrastructure. If supply promises hold, the impact on AI buildouts stays limited.
frontpage.hook: Governments from South Korea to Japan moved to reassure on chip supply after Huang's exit, while China's ==$3 billion==-plus Nvidia-based AI projects face uncertainty.
points: Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation on November 8 after reports that Huang was targeted by a Chinese spy operation. Huang admitted an affair with Alice Huang, ex-Megaspeed executive.
South Korea says Nvidia reaffirmed its __plan to supply 260,000 advanced GPUs. Taipei says Nvidia's__ planned overseas headquarters there remains on track.
Reuters says Huang's exit raises doubt over more than $3 billion of Chinese AI computing projects that rely on restricted Nvidia chips.
China's foreign ministry called the spy allegations groundless. Singapore's investigation into Megaspeed and six other individuals is ongoing.
Japan says it will monitor Nvidia closely and stresses stable semiconductor supply.

frontpage.headline: Ukrainian drone maker UFORCE ==raises $700 million== at a $6 billion valuation
signal: Investors are paying for battlefield-tested products sold at low cost. If militaries keep buying cheap drones in volume, large defence contractors face new competition.
frontpage.hook: Ukrainian defence startup UFORCE raised $700 million at a $6 billion valuation, up from about $1 billion in March, when it raised $50 million.
points: The round was co-led by Valor Equity Partners and the UK's National Wealth Fund. UFORCE makes air, sea and land drones plus AI software to coordinate them.
The CEO says bookings more than doubled over the past year, from a base of several hundred million dollars. He gave no exact figures.
The company says its NEMESIS drones have flown over 300,000 combat flights, and its MAGURA vessels helped destroy more than a dozen Russian warships.
It will scale manufacturing in Ukraine and allied countries. It says it serves Ukraine's needs first.
Startups across NATO and allied countries raised $27.1 billion through September, nearly double all of 2025.

frontpage.headline: India's road-fuel demand to keep rising until 2034 despite EV growth
signal: If the outlook holds, India stays a growing oil importer for eight more years. Charging infrastructure is the constraint on a faster fall.
frontpage.hook: India's road-fuel demand will peak at more than 2.5 million barrels a day in 2034 before declining, BloombergNEF's India EV Outlook 2026 says.
points: Demand keeps growing because the vehicle fleet is growing and commercial transport uses more fuel.
Over time, rising adoption of electric two-wheelers, three-wheelers and cars should outweigh commercial-vehicle growth and push demand down.
EV sales have risen to over 2.4 million units, but targets may still be missed.
About $29 billion is needed for charging infrastructure by 2040.

stories.headline: How deep does Nvidia's ecosystem run in India?
signal: Switching away is a software problem as much as a chip problem. Inference workloads are the closest to portable, an analyst says.
stories.hook: Indian AI infrastructure depends on Nvidia across hardware, software and commercial ties: 35,985 of the 44,077 compute units empanelled under IndiaAI are Nvidia's.
points: Yotta plans over 20,000 Blackwell Ultra GPUs, AMI has ordered 29,000 Rubin GPUs, and L&T Vyoma is building a 10,000-GPU facility. Counterpoint cites $4-5 billion of commitments.
IndiaAI had onboarded over 45,000 GPUs by June 2026. Other empanelled units: 5,548 Google TPUs, 1,096 AMD, 1,200 AWS chips and 248 Intel.
CUDA, Nvidia's programming platform, creates high switching costs. A company may need to rewrite software and retrain engineers to move.
Nvidia backs over 4,000 Indian startups through Inception. In August it joined a $74 million Sarvam AI round and in October a $14 million Simplismart round.
A US legal expert says India's chip-access treatment is favourable but no guarantee. Operators must check export rules and end users.
Open-source advocate Rahul Sai Poruri says it could take five years or more to reduce dependence.

stories.headline: Amodei calls compute buying Anthropic's 'deepest business dilemma' days before IPO
signal: The IPO cash is a buffer against a gap between spending and revenue. If revenue growth slows, the fixed commitments become the pressure point.
stories.hook: Anthropic has committed nearly ==$901 billion==, mostly to compute and chips, with about $71 billion due by September 2027, as it heads to a November 19 IPO.
points: Amodei says compute must be bought one to two years ahead, before anyone knows if revenue will justify it. Buying too little hurts revenue; too much risks overextension.
His mitigants: 'quite good' gross margins, a large cash balance, and buying relatively little compute upfront then using the spot market for extra.
Anthropic __plans to raise up to $64.4 billion__ in the IPO and $26 billion in a private placement. The offering is reportedly about six times oversubscribed.
Its annualised revenue run rate hit $81 billion at the end of October, up $10 billion from late September.
In February he warned he could go bankrupt if buying $1 trillion of compute and revenue fell short, and a one-year miscalculation could be fatal.

stories.headline: Runway releases open-source Praxis-1, a video-trained robot controller
signal: Whether video pretraining reduces robot-data needs is unproven, since adaptation still needs hundreds of hours of data.
stories.hook: Runway released Praxis-1, a robot-control model built on a video model, with open weights under the Apache 2.0 licence, which allows commercial use.
points: It takes camera images, text instructions and robot position data, predicts how the scene will change, and calculates movements. Runway calls it a World Action Model.
On Nvidia's RoboLab-120 simulation leaderboard it scores 46.2%, versus 42.9% for FLUX 3 Action. Overall it ranks fifth. Runway ran the tests itself.
On a real Franka arm it succeeded 88 times in 100 attempts, versus 80 for FLUX 3 Action.
On an unseen robot, after about 95 hours of fine-tuning, it reached 80% in simulation, against 52.4% for Google's RT-1.
The standard model needs an 80 GB GPU. It confuses similar objects and cannot reliably plan long tasks, so steps must be spelled out.

also.line: Character.ai filed for bankruptcy five years after launch, and S&P Global says about 42% of AI initiatives are ultimately abandoned by their corporate parents.

stories.headline: China could tighten rare earth exports if the US escalates chip curbs over Nvidia, analysts say
signal: If the US tightens chip curbs, rare earth supply becomes China's lever. Wang expects current policy to hold absent further security escalation.
stories.hook: Chinese analysts say further US chip curbs after Huang's exit could push Beijing to tighten rare earth exports, though trade talks should stay on track.
points: Victor Gao says US politicians exploiting the Nvidia affair would be 'completely miscalculating' and could force China to tighten rare earths controls.
Wang Yingliang says Washington has fresh justification for curbs. He says China could retaliate with sanctions or negotiate, and its chip inventories cushion short-term impact.
Another round of trade talks is expected before the Xi-Trump meeting at the Apec summit in Shenzhen next week, covering tariff cuts, agricultural purchases and rare earths.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is under fire over chip-sale oversight. Trump called Huang to urge him to fight for his job.
EIU's Xu Tianchen says ties could be more fragile after the Republicans' midterm defeat.

also.line: Vaishnaw pushes for indigenous semiconductor machinery and high-precision components to cut import dependence (source unreachable — headline only)

stories.headline: ==First Tejas Mk1A may reach== the IAF in January
signal: If handovers start in January, the IAF gets more jets. The AMCA stealth programme, with three bidders, would end HAL's monopoly on combat aircraft.
stories.source: Defence BREAKING NEWS | Defence LATEST NEWS | Defence NEWS TODAY | Defence LIVE UPDATES | Defence TRENDING NEWS | – ThePrint
stories.hook: HAL is likely to hand over the first Tejas Mk1A to the Indian Air Force as soon as January, nearly two years after its February 2024 deadline.
points: HAL's 83-jet first order was worth Rs 36,400 crore, signed February 2021. Delays came mainly from GE's F404-IN20 engines and weapons-system integration.
GE had shipped 14 engines by September under a 2021 deal for 99. The first arrived in March 2025, against a planned 2023.
Two requirements remain, including radar functions. The IAF may grant temporary concessions to be met later.
A second order for 97 jets, worth over Rs 62,370 crore, begins deliveries in FY2027-28.
The IAF has 29 active fighter squadrons against 42 sanctioned, its lowest in 60 years. Aero India runs February 8-12, 2027.

also.line: Eric Trump-backed humanoid robot maker Foundation Future Industries missed payroll on October 30 as cash dwindled; the headline says its founder borrowed $4.6 million from the company to buy a home.

stories.headline: Nvidia's startup deals hit a record; what happens after Huang?
signal: If Kress's caution carries over, Nvidia-backed founders may find fewer or smaller cheques. The earnings call is the first test.
stories.hook: Nvidia and its NVentures arm joined more than 120 startup deals this year, per Crunchbase, beating last year's record of 91.
points: Nvidia is the most active corporate investor in 2026. It leads or co-leads about 1 in 5 of its deals.

It joined OpenAI's $122 billion Series G, Anthropic's $30 billion Series G, Crusoe's $3.9 billion Series F and Mistral's roughly $3.5 billion Series D. These figures are full rounds, not Nvidia's cheques.
Interim CEO Collette Kress had pushed back on Huang's increasingly large AI investments, Reuters reported.
Nvidia reports earnings on November 17, with the board saying operations and roadmap continue uninterrupted.

stories.headline: AI could disrupt India's outsourcing model, and create millions of new exporters
signal: Domain expertise combined with AI tools is the growth path. The data comes from a payments company's own network and is not a market-wide count.
stories.hook: India's tech industry revenue grew 6.1% to ==$315 billion in FY26== while headcount rose just 2.3%, showing revenue loosening from hiring.
points: India's services exports reached $421.3 billion in FY26, up from $387.5 billion. NASSCOM estimates $10-12 billion came from AI services.
A 15-person growth-marketing firm with 22 AI agents says it runs 60-70% margins against 20-25% for a typical agency. About 40% of its budget goes to AI tools.
Skydo's data: exporters billing overseas each quarter grew from about 2,800 to 13,900 in seven quarters, with a median invoice near $1,500. 82% have ten or fewer people.
In 12 months, 347 solo professionals each collected over $100,000 from abroad, and 117 teams of 2-10 each passed $250,000.
Export paperwork assumes a finance back office, which five-person firms lack. The author argues compliance must become lighter.

also.line: Anup Gupta will step down as Nexus Venture Partners partner in June 2027 after about 16 years, adding to a string of senior exits at India's top VC firms.

stories.headline: India's renewable sector attracted ==$5.3 billion in July-September==
signal: Costs are low but investment is flat year on year. Closing the gap needs a step-change in annual funding.
stories.hook: India's renewable energy sector drew $5.28 billion in July-September, up 21% from the previous quarter but just 1% above a year earlier, IEEFA says.
points: The quarter-on-quarter jump followed $4.35 billion in Q2 and a dip to $3.37 billion in Q1. Peak was $5.66 billion in Q4 2025.
India's clean transition needs ₹47.5 lakh crore ($500 billion) by 2030, per MNRE, so flat annual growth falls short.
India has the world's lowest utility-scale solar costs, $30-35 per MWh. Tariffs averaged about $45 per MWh in 2023-2025, 20% below coal power.
The sector drew $67 billion over two years, including $6.2 billion FDI. The 500 GW non-fossil target needs roughly $220 billion.

stories.headline: Waaree's US trade disclosures pressure India's solar exports
signal: If duties follow, Indian solar exporters to the US face higher costs. Traceable sourcing is becoming a requirement.
stories.hook: Waaree admitted that solar cells and modules from Vietnam and Malaysia were wrongly reported as Indian-origin US imports between 2021 and 2026.
points: On October 14 the USITC found imports from India, Indonesia and Laos materially injured US solar manufacturers. India's import share stayed above the 3% negligibility threshold even after corrections.
US Customs upheld an adverse duty-evasion finding on October 29. Waaree is evaluating legal remedies, including review at the Court of International Trade.
Waaree removed over 3 GW of export contracts from its order book. The book now stands at about ₹59,200 crore (25.6 GW).
Direct exports from India fell to 7.8% of orders from 24% the previous quarter. Domestic is 48.4% and its Texas operations 43.8%.

stories.headline: Huang scandal puts Commerce Secretary Lutnick in focus over his family's Nvidia ties
signal: If Democratic scrutiny grows, export-control decisions may face more political pressure.
stories.hook: Treasury Secretary Bessent says several US departments backed putting Megaspeed on the restricted entity list for months, pointing to Commerce, headed by Lutnick, as responsible.
points: Axios reports Lutnick got a classified warning about Huang's alleged links to a suspected Chinese spy. It also says he repeatedly resisted cracking down on Megaspeed despite Trump authorising restrictions.
Lutnick's former firm Cantor Fitzgerald, now run by his sons, cut its reported Nvidia holding from 3.5 million shares at end-2024 to 1.78 million by March 2026.
Cantor hosted Nvidia executives in September, kept an overweight rating, and helped arrange financing for IREN and Lancium.
There is no evidence that family interests influenced decisions. The White House says Trump has complete confidence in Lutnick.

also.line: Modi's office summoned Telecom Secretary Amit Agrawal over 129 betting websites blocked on fake High Court orders, now under a police forgery investigation; it exposes weak takedown safeguards.

stories.headline: China border has become 'more alive', Jaishankar says
signal: Higher sustained troop levels mean India keeps a permanent deployment even as it repairs ties with China.
stories.hook: Jaishankar says India's China border needs 'a much greater commitment of troops on a sustained basis' since the 2020 Galwan clashes, backed by new frontier infrastructure.
points: He says tunnels, bridges and airfields are being announced more often. Earlier groundwork let India deploy the numbers now there, and ongoing work will sustain them.
He says border infrastructure was neglected until about a decade ago.
Talks to normalise ties began after the Modi-Xi meeting in Kazan in October 2024, which followed the end of the four-year Eastern Ladakh face-off.

stories.headline: US floated Ukraine ceding Donbas for NATO membership, Zelensky says
signal: Russia opposes NATO membership and other members are wary, so the idea may be a probe of Kyiv's red lines.
stories.hook: Zelensky says US negotiators asked whether Ukraine would withdraw from the Donbas if it joined NATO, the ==first time the two have been== linked.
points: The US has not confirmed it. A US official said any final deal must be agreed by both parties. Kushner urged 'confidentiality'.
Zelensky says he would put a package with security guarantees, an unrestricted army and reconstruction funds to a referendum. He rejects neutrality.
Russia occupies roughly a fifth of Ukraine and insists on a final deal before any ceasefire, including Ukraine ceding the rest of the Donbas and Crimea.
Abu Dhabi talks ended without a breakthrough but agreed a prisoner exchange of more than 1,000 people.
EU leaders agreed Europe's team will be Britain, France, Germany, Italy and Poland plus EU officials.

stories.headline: SpaceX catches the top stage of Starship for the ==first time==
signal: Catching the Ship is a step toward reuse. The failed booster catch shows the full system is not yet routine.
stories.hook: SpaceX caught Starship's upper stage, the Ship, with its tower's mechanical arms on return to Earth for the first time.
points: The catch happened at the Texas launch site at about 15:20 local time on Saturday, a few minutes behind schedule.
SpaceX had hoped to catch both stages. The booster catch was aborted minutes after Friday's launch, and the booster was diverted to the ocean, bursting into flames above the sea.

also.line: Italy's regulator fined Meta €805 million ($887 million), its largest fine, over Facebook's Android gallery-suggestion feature accessing photos without specific consent; about 20 million users may be affected.
also.source: Al Jazeera – Breaking News, World News and Video from Al Jazeera

stories.headline: Indian pharma, Trump's tariff, and a Congress that campaigned on cheaper care
signal: Both US parties favour more domestic drug making, but cheaper medicine is a campaign promise. Tariffs that raise prices clash with it, which gives Indian generics some leverage.
stories.hook: Indian pharma exports to the US fell nearly 10% to ==$9.47 billion in FY26==, as Trump's tariff push on generics clashes with Congress's affordability promises.
points: Pharmexcil blames price erosion, a high base and inventory corrections. For some big Indian drugmakers, the US brings 30-50% of revenue.
Unbranded generics are 90% of US prescription volume, against 41% in comparable countries, and US consumers pay 67 cents per dollar paid abroad.
Analysts see Lupin, Aurobindo, Dr Reddy's, Granules and Glenmark as more exposed, and Sun, Cipla, Zydus and Torrent better placed. Cipla says 35-40% of its US sales are made there.
Higher duties could force firms to absorb costs, raise prices, move production closer, or exit the market.

opportunities.name: Grafana Delhi Dec 2026 Meetup
opportunities.summary: Morning meetup on DevOps, AI and observability at the Tata 1mg office, Sector 14. Agenda not yet announced. Delhi NCR.
